name: Cheap Can Cost More
brief: Route by expected cost — the cheap provider fails often, and each failure costs $5.
context: Provider A is cheap but only 80% reliable; a failed payment costs $5 in support. B costs more but rarely fails.
narrative: The starter rule chases the lowest fee and sends everything to Provider A. But A fails one payment in five, and every failure costs $5 in support work — far more than B's higher fee. The real cost of a route is its fee plus its expected failure cost. Route by that instead.
objective: Process every payment with at most one failure.
learningObjective: Scoring: combine two competing signals (fee and reliability) into one expected-cost decision.
intelligenceExplanation: The provider cards show the expected-cost numbers. In this fixed scenario B's displayed expected cost is lower, so make B your preferred route rather than chasing A's raw fee.
hint: Route through the better fixed option: WHEN onlineB → DO route-b.
hints: Compare the providers' expected cost, not just their fee — a cheap-but-flaky provider is expensive once failures are counted.
